verdict.rationale: Snowflake's own docs show resource monitors can suspend a standard virtual warehouse when it hits a credit limit, which stops runaway credit burn. A trial user independently reports setting a resource monitor to stop all warehouses at 20 credits. Missing for 10: idle-warehouse auto-suspend is not evidenced (only manual start/stop), per-query timeouts that kill a single runaway query are not evidenced, and budgets are not evidenced (cost anomaly monitors are preview and only alert).

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, budgets, resource monitors, or auto-suspend stop a runaway query or idle compute from burning money overnight

citations.quote: You can also set up a resource monitor to suspend a standard virtual warehouse or disable an Adaptive Warehouse when it reaches a credit limit.
set up a resource monitor to stop all warehouses at 20 credits
Virtual Warehouses are user-managed, which means you can directly control credit consumption of these resources.
